mandatory_stop_after_deployment.rule: Once the requested fix is deployed, stop immediately. Under no circumstances perform further tool/function calls, live checks, browser checks, tests, scans, screenshots, verification, cleanup, research, extra fixes, or memory/checkpoint updates as part of that deployment task. Complete necessary checks and any already-authorized checkpoint preparation before deployment. Do not add post-deployment work under an 'essential check', 'final verification', or 'just saving memory' exception. Give only a brief completion message. Further work requires a new explicit user request.
mandatory_stop_after_deployment.supersedes: All earlier post-deployment verification, audit, read-back and automatic checkpoint requirements.

execution_efficiency_preference.rule: Keep work limited to the current request. Reuse the accepted source and completed evidence. Run only an existing required gate or a focused check addressing a concrete risk introduced by this change. Do not add optional suites, simulations, screenshots, broad audits, repeated research or automatic checkpoint work. known_blocker_efficiency.source: Explicit user correction after a known GitLab CI quota blocker was retried without evidence of recovery.
rules: Before substantial implementation or deployment work, check already-known failure points and the required completion path using existing evidence first. Use only the smallest read-only check needed if the state is genuinely unknown.

Do not retry a known quota, permission, missing-runtime, or unavailable-service failure without new evidence that its cause has changed. Repeated requests, elapsed time alone, or a new session do not establish recovery.

When a blocker prevents a requested outcome, report it promptly and stop only the dependent operation. Continue useful independent work already authorized. Explicit manual HTML delivery remains authorized while CI or deployment is blocked; no repeated permission is needed for that handoff.
Use an already-authorized, supported alternative only when evidence shows it can complete the task. Never bypass CI, access controls or approvals, or incur costs to avoid reporting a blocker.
Reuse prepared changes, prior focused checks and compact checkpoints. Do not repeat discovery, simulations, tests, broad file reads or unchanged memory updates.
Keep tool output bounded to decision-relevant fields. Do not dump full registries, repository trees, large files or minified code when a targeted read suffices.
Unexpected failures cannot be ruled out. Report actual limitations honestly; never promise failure-free execution or claim an attempted action succeeded.

known_blocker_example.resume_condition: Evidence that GitLab CI quota or runner capacity has been restored; do not blindly retry.
